sections.label: S&P 500 intangible asset value
sections.summary: 90% of the value of S&P 500 companies today lies in their IA.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: In fact, 90% of the value of S&P 500 companies today lies in their IA.

sections.label: Intellectual Property Amendment Bill statutes
sections.summary: The Intellectual Property (Amendment) Bill changes the Patents Act, Trade Marks Act, Registered Designs Act, Plant Varieties Protection Act and Geographical Indications Act 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Today's Intellectual Property (Amendment) Bill makes changes to many of the IP statutes, specifically, the Patents Act, the Trade Marks Act, the Registered Designs Act, the Plant Varieties Protection Act and the Geographical Indications Act 2014.

sections.label: Partial acceptance of trademark applications
sections.summary: Clauses 43, 44, 46, 47, 52 and 53 let IPOS partially accept applications, benefiting up to about 13% of domestic applications.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clauses 43, 44, 46, 47, 52 and 53 of the Bill will amend the Trade Marks Act to allow IPOS to partially accept an application, allowing the trademark to be registered for those goods and services for which there were no objections in such cases.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: We expect that the change to permit partial acceptance for national applications will benefit up to about 13% of these domestic applications.

sections.label: Publishing requests for corrections
sections.summary: The Bill gives IPOS discretion to publish correction requests so third parties can assess whether to oppose them.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: The Bill will amend the relevant Acts to give IPOS the discretion to publish requests for corrections, so that third parties are made aware of such correction requests and can assess whether they wish to oppose the corrections.

sections.label: Shorter period for minor patent amendments
sections.summary: Clause 10 lets examiners invite applicants to make minor amendments within a shorter period, avoiding written opinions and reducing turnaround times.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 10 changes this so that if an examiner's objections can be overcome with minor amendments to the specification of the patent application, examiners can then simply invite applicants to make those amendments within a shorter period of time.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This will obviate the need to issue a written opinion, thereby reducing turnaround and processing times for part of the 5,000 substantive examination requests that IPOS expects to receive annually.

sections.label: Time saved on patent applications
sections.summary: This saves time and effort for up to 800 patent applications per year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This is more direct; it gets to the point.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: This will save time and effort for up to 800 patent applications per year.

sections.label: IPOS patent sequence listing rules
sections.summary: IPOS intends to amend Patents Act rules to require sequence listings with patent applications where applicable.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Moving forward, IPOS intends to amend the rules made under the Patents Act to require sequence listings to be filed with patent applications, where applicable.

sections.label: Expired trademarks as earlier trade marks
sections.summary: Clause 41 amends the Trade Marks Act so expired trademarks count as earlier trade marks while eligible for renewal or restoration.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Clause 41 will therefore amend the Trade Marks Act to clarify that expired trademarks will be considered "earlier trade marks" for as long as they remain eligible for renewal or restoration.

sections.label: Bill implementation and IP hub
sections.summary: The Bill amends how intellectual property rights are registered in Singapore, with majority implementation intended by May 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: If passed, we intend to implement the majority of the Bill by May 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill amends how intellectual property rights are registered in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This strengthens our position as a global IP hub and brings us closer to Singapore's IP Strategy 2030.

sections.label: IP Strategy 2030 and environment
sections.summary: IP Strategy 2030 can help protect the environment and fight climate change across a wide range of IP classes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, our IP Strategy 2030 can play an important role in protecting the environment and fighting climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Innovation and technology has the potential to help us lead more sustainable lives and adapt to a changing world.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These changes relate to a wide range of IP classes, including patents, registered designs, trade marks, geographical indications and plant varieties protection.

sections.label: Partial refusal mechanism trade mark friction
sections.summary: The partial refusal mechanism is more efficient, but institutional frictions may inhibit excessively frivolous trade mark applications.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In particular, while the partial refusal mechanism is certainly more efficient from the perspective of expediting legal processes involved, institutional frictions may yet serve a purpose to inhibit excessively frivolous trade mark applications.

sections.label: Time periods shifted to rules
sections.summary: The Bill shifts stipulated time periods from the Act to the rules across multiple IP classes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Bill itself proposes that the stipulated time periods be shifted from the Act to the rules across multiple IP classes as captured in amendments to section 35, excuse me, 36 of the Patents Act, section 19 of the Trade Marks Act, section 21 of the Registered Designs Act and section 51 of the Geographical Indications Act.

sections.label: Patents Act open data amendments
sections.summary: Amendments to section 108 of the Patents Act require published patents be made available to the public, supplementing open data practices like the Patents Open Dossier database.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Amendments to section 108 of the Patents Act also touch on another element of information technology, namely, the requirement that published patents be made available to public.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I believe that these amendments supplement existing open data practices, notably, the launch of the Patents Open Dossier (POD) database in June 2017, something that Minister Edwin Tong also spoke on earlier.

sections.label: IPOS database search and Bill scope
sections.summary: A question asks if the Minister will share IPOS efforts to develop the database for keyword or categorical searches; the Bill amends five Acts, excluding the Copyright Act.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, I wonder if the Minister will be willing to share their efforts by IPOS to further develop the database to allow for, say keyword or categorical searches so as to make it more useful.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The substantial amendments tabled in this Bill span five existing Acts and exclude the Copyright Act, which was debated last year.

sections.label: Plant Varieties Protection Act examination
sections.summary: The new section 18A of the Plant Varieties Protection Act introduces an additional mode of examination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The new section 18A of the Plant Varieties Protection Act introduces an additional mode of examination.

sections.label: New breeder's test mode
sections.summary: The new breeder's test mode lets breeders perform required tests themselves or engage someone recognised by the Registrar or appointed Examiner before submitting results to IPOS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The new breeder’s test mode will give the applicant another manner in which the application can proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, breeders can now opt to perform the required tests by themselves, or to directly engage someone else recognised by the Registrar or the appointed Examiner to do so, before submitting the results to IPOS.

sections.label: Public research and IP Fast Track
sections.summary: Unlocking public sector research benefits businesses, and the Singapore IP Fast Track programme introduced in 2020 expedites patents, trade marks and registered designs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Unlocking the fruits of public sector research will benefit our businesses, even as their work in bringing research to the market helps realise the potential of these innovations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And, finally, the Singapore IP Fast Track programme, introduced in 2020, expedites the processing of IP applications – whether they are patents, trade marks and registered designs, they can move from application to protection in as fast as six, three and one month respectively.

sections.label: IP system fostering innovation
sections.summary: You cannot misrepresent a product's basis or source; the IP system fosters innovation and commercialisation, including green technologies, helping new ideas and innovators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is just that you cannot misrepresent the basis or the source of your product.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, competition is not stifled but innovation is protected under our current regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will continue to ensure that our IP system fosters innovation, promotes commercialisation – and that includes in spaces like in green technologies – and helps new ideas, new innovators realise their potential.

sections.label: Reviewing Singapore IP regime
sections.summary: MinLaw and IPOS will continue to review, update and improve Singapore's IP regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: MinLaw and IPOS will continue to work to review, update and improve Singapore’s IP regime.

sections.label: Trade mark classes and innovators
sections.summary: Different classes are dealt with in different legislation, and restricting trade marks affects innovators and inventors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I had understood Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There are different classes and that is precisely why we have dealt with it in different pieces of legislation, recognising that there are different intrinsic qualities that go behind each of these classes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If we try to reduce the space or the recognition of trade marks or curtail them or compromise them, then the knock-on impact on innovators and inventors wanting to bring their products into Singapore to obtain that protection will be in turn affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And that was the broader point that I made – about sounding a caution about trying to restrict the application of trade marks for these innovations.      .
